title: Model Question Paper 2
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–20 carry 1 mark each; questions 21–35 carry 2 marks each.
Section B: 2-mark answers in 30–50 words, 3-mark answers in 50–80 words, 6-mark answers in 80–120 words. Map questions carry 4 marks.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions (2 parts of 1 mark, or 4 parts of ½ mark).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Imperialism is the practice of extending control over the ____ and economic life of another country. The country which is conquered is called a ____.
Fill in the blanks: Farmers were forced to grow ____ on 3/20th part of their land. The first passenger railway ran from Bombay to ____ in 1853.
Fill in the blanks: The formation of the two ____ at Amritsar and Lahore in the 1870s was the beginning of the ____ reform movement among the Sikhs.
Fill in the blanks: At Kanpur ____ was declared the Peshwa, and his troops were commanded by ____ and Azimullah.
True or False: (a) The Simon Commission had no Indian member. (b) The Muslim League was founded at Lucknow in 1916.
questions.answer: (a) True (b) False — it was founded at Dacca in 1906 (the Lucknow Pact was in 1916).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: The highest peak of the Eastern Ghats is ____ and the ____ hills join the Western and Eastern Ghats in the south.

questions.answer: (a) True (b) False — it is a rain-shadow area and receives less rain.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Mention any two features of Fascism.
questions.answer: (1) Hostility to democracy and socialism, with the aim of establishing a dictatorship (Mussolini banned all other parties). (2) It glorified war and extreme nationalism and used terror and violence against opponents.

questions.q: Mention two legal measures which helped improve the status of women in British India.
questions.answer: (1) Sati was banned in 1829 by Lord Bentinck. (2) The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act of 1856 allowed widows to remarry. (The Sharda Act of 1929 also prevented child marriage.)

questions.q: Describe two main functions of the Chief Minister.
questions.answer: (1) The Chief Minister advises the Governor on appointing ministers, allocates portfolios, presides over the Council of Ministers and coordinates ministers. (2) He/she is the sole link between the Council of Ministers and the Governor, communicating all decisions and legislative proposals, and guides the State's policies.

questions.q: Describe any two powers of the Prime Minister related to the Council of Ministers.
questions.answer: (1) The President appoints ministers and allocates portfolios on the PM's recommendation, so the PM makes and unmakes the Council. (2) The PM presides over Cabinet meetings and coordinates ministers; if the PM resigns the whole Council stands dissolved.

questions.q: Why do GDP and per capita income not effectively measure the quality of people's life?
questions.answer: GDP ignores leisure, environmental quality, freedom, social justice and gender equality. Per capita income is only an average and does not show inequality of income, so it cannot tell whether the benefits of development reach the poor and disadvantaged.

questions.q: How does the new notion of security differ from the traditional notion? Give two points.
questions.answer: (1) The traditional notion is about military threats to a nation's territory and sovereignty; the new one covers threats like terrorism, hunger, disease, environmental damage and denial of human rights. (2) The new notion focuses on individuals and humankind, not just States, and treats security as a precondition of development and dignity.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the system of alliances which developed in Europe before the First World War.
questions.answer: In 1882 Germany, Austria and Italy formed the Triple Alliance, promising mutual military help. In 1907 England, Russia and France formed the Triple Entente. Europe was divided into two hostile camps; they competed in producing deadly weapons, and mutual hatred and suspicion meant any small conflict would draw all of Europe into war.

questions.q: Explain the impact of the British education policy on India.
questions.answer: (1) English was introduced to create cheap clerks and a loyal class; the Charter Act of 1813 and Wood's Despatch (1854) led to English schools and universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras (1857). (2) Mass and elementary education was neglected; education became a monopoly of the rich and city dwellers. (3) But English became a link language and Western ideas of liberty, equality and democracy spread, producing reformers and nationalists.

questions.q: Describe any three main features of the hot weather season in India.
questions.answer: (1) From March to May temperatures rise in the plains, west and central India, and a low-pressure monsoon trough forms from Jaisalmer to Odisha. (2) Hot, dry winds called 'loo' blow over the northern plains and dust storms occur in the north-west. (3) Local thunderstorms — Kaal Baisakhi in West Bengal — and pre-monsoon mango showers in Kerala and Karnataka occur.

questions.q: Why is there a dense rail network in the Gangetic plain but not in hilly and desert areas? Explain.
questions.answer: (1) The Gangetic plain is level, so railways are easy and cheap to build; hills and deserts make construction difficult and costly. (2) The plain is the food bowl of India and densely populated, so there is heavy movement of goods and people. (3) It has many large cities and industries, while deserts and hills have few people and little economic activity.

questions.q: What are the goals of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan?
questions.answer: (1) Enrolment of all children of 6–14 years in school or alternative centres. (2) Bridging gender and social category gaps at the primary and elementary levels. (3) Universal retention and elementary education of satisfactory quality with emphasis on education for life.

questions.q: What are the causes of the Naxalite movement? How can it be solved?
questions.answer: Causes: social discrimination and economic deprivation of tribals, SCs and dalits; the fruits of development not reaching them; disputes over land and forests. Solutions: faster development — roads, schools, jobs — in affected areas; land reforms and protection of forest rights; dialogue to bring youth into the mainstream along with firm action against violence.

questions.q: On the given outline map of India, mark and shade: (A) an area receiving above 200 cm rainfall on the west coast (B) the area of Gujarat receiving less than 60 cm rainfall per annum (C) the Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills (D) the region of the Bay of Bengal where cyclones occur in October–November.
questions.answer: (A) The narrow strip along the Western Ghats/west coast from south Gujarat to Kerala (Konkan and Malabar coasts). (B) Kachchh and northern Saurashtra in western Gujarat. (C) Meghalaya, south of Assam. (D) The northern and western Bay of Bengal off the coasts of Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu (Mahanadi, Godavari and Krishna deltas).

questions.q: On the given outline map of India, mark and label: (A) a port in West Bengal (B) Kempe Gowda International Airport (C) a major port in Odisha (D) the westernmost terminal city of the Golden Quadrilateral.
questions.answer: (A) Haldia (or Kolkata) — on the Hugli near its mouth. (B) Bengaluru, Karnataka. (C) Paradip — on the Odisha coast near the Mahanadi delta. (D) Mumbai, Maharashtra.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: How did the Policy of Appeasement and the rise of Fascism lead to the Second World War?
questions.answer: (1) Germany was humiliated by the Treaty of Versailles and wanted revenge; Italy was angry at getting no colonies. (2) Fascism under Mussolini and Nazism under Hitler glorified war and promised to restore lost glory by conquest. (3) Germany annexed the Rhineland (1936), Austria and Czechoslovakia (1938); Italy attacked Ethiopia. (4) Britain and France, wanting to check communism, followed the Policy of Appeasement and allowed this — the Munich Pact of 1938 gave Hitler the Sudetenland. (5) Germany, Italy and Japan formed the Rome–Berlin–Tokyo Axis. (6) When Germany attacked Poland on 1 September 1939, Britain declared war and World War II began.

questions.q: Explain the powers and position of the Governor of a State.
questions.answer: (1) Executive powers: appoints the Chief Minister and ministers, the Advocate General and heads of State commissions. (2) Legislative powers: summons, prorogues and dissolves the legislature, addresses it, nominates members, and assents to or returns bills or reserves them for the President. (3) Financial powers: the budget is presented on his/her behalf, no money bill without recommendation, controls the Contingency Fund. (4) Discretionary powers: chooses the CM when no party has a majority, reserves bills for the President, and reports for President's Rule under Article 356. (5) Position: normally a nominal head who acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the CM. (6) But he/she becomes effective in political instability and as the link between the Centre and the State, so is more than a ceremonial head.
